sources.title: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville, Deep Learning, Chapter 10, full online textbook chapter
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 10 HTML; specifically §§10.1–10.2 on recurrent computation and unrolling, §10.10 and §10.10.1 on gated recurrent networks and LSTM equations (Eqs. 10.40–10.44, printed pp. 405–406). The full chapter was fetched; these are the inspected mathematical passages.

contents.name: §10.1, Unfolding Computational Graphs: finite time-indexed copies of a shared recurrent computation
contents.reason: The definition states a finite horizon, one time-indexed map per step, and shared parameters without importing the chapter's gradient claims.

contents.name: §10.2, Recurrent Neural Networks: recurrent hidden-state update and parameter sharing over time
contents.reason: The local definition specifies state, input, initial value, horizon and parameter reuse as the source's recurrent convention requires.

contents.name: §10.10.1, Long Short-Term Memory: input, forget, output and candidate equations (Eqs. 10.40–10.44)
contents.reason: The item preserves the peephole-free equations, domains, shared parameters and activation conventions used in this source treatment.

contents.name: Chapter 10 sections on gradient propagation, bidirectional/recursive variants, and empirical model comparisons beyond the assigned architecture statements
contents.reason: The assigned pair defines recurrent and LSTM architectures only; it states no gradient theorem, bidirectional or recursive architecture, training method, or empirical comparison, so adding those claims would exceed the controlling design.

sources.title: Albert Gu, Karan Goel, and Christopher Ré, Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces, arXiv:2111.00396 v3
sources.locator: Full 32-page arXiv v3 text inspected. Relevant headings and arguments: §§2.1–2.4, §§3.1–3.3, Theorems 1–3, Algorithm 1, Appendix C.1–C.3 (including Lemmas C.2–C.4 and Proposition 5).

contents.name: §2.1, State Space Models: continuous state equation, output and separate direct term
contents.reason: The local definition gives finite-dimensional domains, local integrability, absolutely continuous trajectories and the separate direct term.

contents.name: §2.2, Addressing Long-Range Dependencies with HiPPO: motivation and empirical context
contents.reason: This pair proves finite matrix structure but makes no memory-optimality, long-range-accuracy or benchmark claim; the motivating discussion is not needed as a mathematical prerequisite.

contents.name: §2.3, Discrete-time SSM: bilinear recurrent matrices and Theorem 2's recurrence-cost claim
contents.reason: The bilinear definition states the required inverse condition; the local DPLR theorem supplies the actual solve and its correction invertibility.

contents.name: §2.4, Training SSMs: unrolled zero-state recurrence and convolution kernel
contents.reason: The zero-state kernel is stated with the column-vector and conjugate-transpose convention, and its recurrent/convolutional equality is verified locally in a scalar example.

contents.name: §3.1, Motivation: Diagonalization; Lemma 3.1 on state-coordinate equivalence and Lemma 3.2 on the raw HiPPO diagonalizer
contents.reason: The theorem proves the needed coordinate equivalence directly and explicitly uses a diagonal similarity for LegT; it does not import the source's ill-conditioned raw diagonalizer as an S4 representation.

contents.name: §3.2, The S4 Parameterization: Definition 1 and Theorem 1 on normal-plus-low-rank form for HiPPO matrices
contents.reason: Entrywise decompositions for LegS, LegT and LagT are supplied locally, then the finite-dimensional complex spectral theorem produces the DPLR coordinates.

contents.name: §3.3, S4 Algorithms and Computational Complexity: Theorem 2 and Theorem 3
contents.reason: Theorem 2's one-step claim is proved with both the ordinary Woodbury and singular-diagonal bordered solve branches.

contents.name: §3.3, S4 Algorithms and Computational Complexity: four Cauchy products, linear space, and the source-reported numerical precision claim in Theorem 3
contents.reason: Original source operation claim is preserved with a complete local arc-tree numerical supplier and S4 error propagation. Absolute kernel error epsilon has explicit log(kappa/epsilon) dependence, reducing uniformly to the reported log(1/epsilon) factor on bounded-kappa families. Variable-precision scalar words/operations are counted, with separation-dependent precision and no bit-cost claim.

contents.name: Appendix C.1: normal-plus-low-rank structure of the HiPPO LegS matrix
contents.reason: The LegS skew-symmetric part and rank-one correction are checked entry by entry, with the source's time-dependent 1/t coefficient factor retained.

contents.name: Appendix C.2: bilinear update, explicit DPLR solve, and Woodbury identity
contents.reason: The finite-dimensional Woodbury identity and its two-sided inverse formula are proved locally; the DPLR cost theorem also handles a singular diagonal base.

contents.name: Appendix C.3, Reductions 1–3 and Lemmas C.2–C.4: truncated generating function, bilinear resolvent and Cauchy-kernel reduction
contents.reason: The finite geometric identity, bilinear resolvent algebra, Woodbury correction, root −1 value and exceptional eigenvalue limit are derived locally.

contents.name: Appendix C.3, Proposition 5 and Corollary C.5: exact and numerical Cauchy-kernel cost statements
contents.reason: The exact arithmetic complexity is proved by the local product-tree/FFT argument; Proposition 5's numerical branch is not treated as proof of the S4 finite-precision claim.

contents.name: §4 and Appendix D: datasets, benchmarks, training protocols and empirical performance results
contents.reason: The assignment excludes empirical performance, long-context accuracy and complete training-cost claims; the source's experiments are not used as theorem evidence.

sources.title: Albert Gu, Tri Dao, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, and Christopher Ré, HiPPO: Recurrent Memory with Optimal Polynomial Projections, arXiv:2008.07669 v2
sources.locator: Full relevant sections inspected: §2.3 for the LegS, LegT and LagT coefficient/state generators; Appendices D.1–D.3 for their matrix formulas and derivations. The item uses the finite matrix calculations only.

contents.name: §2.3, HiPPO matrices: LegS, LegT and LagT generator conventions and entries
contents.reason: The theorem records each matrix's entry convention and proves the stated normal-plus-rank-one or rank-two decomposition.

contents.name: Appendix D.1: LegS coefficient matrix and its skew-symmetric plus rank-one decomposition
contents.reason: The local proof preserves the exact diagonal and off-diagonal entries and states that the ODE carries the additional time factor 1/t.

contents.name: Appendices D.2–D.3: LegT and LagT state matrices and their coordinate conventions
contents.reason: The proof distinguishes original LagT diagonal −1 from the S4 paper's −1/2 variant and handles LegT by an explicit invertible diagonal similarity.

contents.name: The polynomial-projection optimality and approximation results beyond the finite matrix decompositions
contents.reason: The assigned theorem concerns matrix form and coordinate changes only; no optimal-projection or approximation-performance conclusion is asserted or needed for the DPLR algorithm.

contents.name: §§3.2–3.3: polynomial multiplication and exact Cauchy computations through polynomial arithmetic

contents.name: §6.1 geometric separated-kernel expansion, developed into a complete local root-arc-tree proof
contents.reason: The local proof supplies certified overlapping routing, constant per-depth interaction lists, degree streaming with linear word memory independent of expansion degree, explicit geometric remainder, and a finite circuit rounding bound for all noncollision root-grid inputs.
